id_rural_wall.blurb: Rural Wall is a compact sport wall at Massacre Rocks near American Falls in eastern Idaho, standing a short distance to the right of the All American Wall. Nearly all of its 24 lines are bolted sport routes, with one top-rope and one trad line mixed in. The grades lean toward the middle and upper-middle range: a few easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9, a solid core of 5.10s and 5.11s, and a single 5.12. That makes it a good fit for climbers who already lead 5.10 and want a focused wall to work through, and less so for brand-new leaders.
id_rural_wall.approach: About a 15 minute walk from the parking area on the west rim.

id_02_the_head_wall.blurb: The Head Wall is a steep basalt wall in the Teddy Bear Cove sport area, west of American Falls in eastern Idaho. All 23 routes are bolted. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with one 5.8 and a couple of 5.9s for warming up. Thin bands of crumbly rock between thick sections of solid basalt form roofs, so a typical line has two or three overhanging steps and rewards big, powerful moves on large holds. The wall faces southwest, giving shade in the morning and sun through the afternoon. Reach it by walking in from the neighbouring crags on either side.

id_decadent_wall.blurb: Decadent Wall is one of the best-known walls in the Breadloaves, the upper part of City of Rocks National Reserve in southern Idaho; climbers have used the name since the late 1980s. It is mostly a trad wall, with a handful of bolted sport lines mixed in. The grade spread is unusually wide: a couple of very easy lines around 5.4 to 5.6, a good group of moderates from 5.7 to 5.9, and a steady run of 5.10s through 5.12. The granite face looks west and sits only a short stroll from the parking lot, so it suits mixed groups of different abilities.
